name: Threat Modeling
description: Systematic identification and prioritization of threats to a system, application, or process. Encompasses understanding what is being built, what can go wrong, and what to do about it — independent of any single methodology or framework.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to threat modeling concepts

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the purpose and basic structure of threat modeling
evidence: Can explain why threat modeling is performed and when it adds value
Understands the general flow: scope definition, threat identification, mitigation planning
Aware that multiple methodologies and diagramming approaches exist

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can participate in and contribute to a threat modeling exercise with guidance
evidence: Contributes meaningful threats during facilitated sessions
Can decompose a system into components, trust boundaries, and data flows
Produces threat model documentation reviewed and approved by senior staff

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently conducts threat modeling for systems of moderate complexity
evidence: Selects and applies an appropriate approach based on the target system
Identifies threats across relevant categories without significant gaps
Produces actionable threat models that inform design and testing decisions
Integrates threat modeling outputs into engagement planning or development lifecycle

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Facilitates threat modeling for complex or novel systems; coaches others through the process
evidence: Leads threat modeling for multi-component or cross-domain systems
Adapts approach to the audience and system type (embedded, cloud, protocol, etc.)
Reviews and improves threat models produced by others
Connects threat model findings to concrete test plans and security architecture recommendations

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's threat modeling practice; advances methodology for novel problem domains
evidence: Established or significantly evolved the lab's threat modeling practice
Develops custom approaches for domains where standard methodologies fall short
Trains teams and embeds threat modeling into organizational processes
Recognized externally for threat modeling expertise

assessment_methods.description: Review threat model artifacts from 2-3 recent engagements for completeness, accuracy, and actionability
Given an unfamiliar system architecture, produce a threat model covering scope, decomposition, threat identification, and prioritized mitigations
Observe facilitation of a threat modeling session with a cross-functional group
